primary.title: The Akbarnama
primary.author: Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak
primary.rationale: This is the official biography of Akbar, commissioned by Akbar himself and written by his courtier Abu'l-Fazl. It is a foundational primary source for understanding Akbar's reign, policies, and personal life.

primary.title: Ain-i-Akbari
primary.author: Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak
primary.rationale: Part of the Akbarnama, this work provides detailed information on Akbar's administration, economy, culture, and laws. It is an indispensable primary source for the administrative and social history of the Mughal Empire under Akbar.

secondary.title: Akbar: The Great Mughal
secondary.author: J.L. Mehta
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and scholarly biography of Akbar, analyzing his political, administrative, and religious policies. It is a well-regarded academic work.

secondary.title: Akbar and the Temples of Gujarat
secondary.author: Sunita Singh
secondary.rationale: This article examines Akbar's policies towards religious sites in Gujarat, offering insights into his religious tolerance and administrative practices in a specific region. It is a peer-reviewed academic article.

secondary.title: The Mughal Empire: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: John F. Richards
secondary.rationale: While a broad overview of the Mughal Empire, this book provides significant context and analysis of Akbar's reign as a pivotal period. It is published by Oxford University Press, a major academic press.

suggestions.notes: Akbar himself did not author extensive personal writings that survive in a readily accessible format. His biography and administrative records were compiled by his court historians, primarily Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak, and these serve as the most important primary sources.
